courses.subject: CSAT
courses.title: Technological Practices in Arts and Design
courses.description: This course provides students with foundational knowledge and hands-on experience in the application of technology in arts and design practice. Through workshops and prototyping, students will learn different digital media techniques and experiment with producing prototypes using methods introduced in the course. By engaging directly with technology in a guided process and peer discussions, students will develop insights on how technology transforms artistic expression and design practice, fostering awareness of sustainability, ethics, and collaboration in design practice.
courses.academic_group: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
courses.academic_org: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, students will be able to:
1. Explain how technology can support and transform contemporary arts and design practice across different creative contexts.
2. Explore and apply a range of creative methods and processes that integrate concept development, experimentation, and making.
3. Demonstrate basic proficiency in developing prototype solutions or creative outcomes that illustrate how ideas translate into material/process and experience.
4. Critically assess the creative, ethical, and sustainable dimensions of technology-mediated arts and design work.
5. Collaborate effectively and communicate ideas clearly in the development and presentation of art-tech projects.
courses.course_syllabus:
(For reference only. Subject to change)

[course format]
This course will be workshop-based with short lectures to introduce basic concepts and skills. Students will work in small groups with regular in-class tutorials and design reviews.

[course components]
- Topical Lectures and Case Studies: technology in contemporary art and design

- Skills/Tech Tools Workshops (may include but not limited to): UI/UX (Figma, Flowstep); Creative Coding (TouchDesigner); 3D scanning/modelling (Blender, TripoAI); AIGC Tools

- Prototype Lab Sessions
- Work-in-progress Discussions
- Project Showcase

courses.subject: CSAT
courses.title: Field Study in Arts Technology
courses.description: This course aims to broaden students’ perspectives through a field study focused on arts and technology, creative industries, and related institutions or sites. It combines thematic seminars, workshops, field research, documentation and report to cultivate their interests and analytical capacity. A different topic and destination will be selected each year to reflect current development in art/tech practice, where students will undertake a design research project that includes on-site observation and engagement with cultural professionals and institutions to connect classroom learning with real-world creative practice.
courses.academic_group: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
courses.academic_org: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing the course, students will be able to:
1. Conduct field-based research on arts and technology, creative industries, or related cultural institutions and practices.
2. Analyse how institutions, technologies, audiences, and contexts shape contemporary arts and technology practice.
3. Use observation, documentation, interviews, and reflective inquiry to build an informed understanding of a selected topic in arts/technology
4. Evaluate selected cases and site-based examples with attention to cultural context, innovation, sustainability, and ethical considerations.
5. Communicate research findings through a coherent project, report, presentation, or prototype informed by primary evidence
6. Demonstrate awareness of global trends and cross-cultural perspectives in arts, technology, and related spatial practices.
courses.course_syllabus:
(For reference only. Subject to change)

This course comprises seminars on creative research methods, a field trip, and project development. The specific content and structure will vary according to the selected theme and field study destination.

[1] Introduction to Art/Tech Field Study Methods
- Overview of current arts and technology practice
- Approaches to field research, documentation, and analysis
- Ethical considerations in fieldwork

[2] Theme‑Specific Seminars & Workshops
- Lectures/seminars on selected art/tech topic
- Case studies of relevant artists or institutions
- Training on field research tools/technologies (e.g., photogrammetry, audio-visual documentation)
- Research design and project proposal development

[3] Field Study Activities
- Visits to art‑tech labs/studios, creative agencies, institutions
- On‑site observation, interviews, data gathering, and experiential learning

[4] Independent Project
- Guided inquiry into a topic related to the year’s theme
- Presentation of findings and critical reflection on art/tech implications to cultural, creative, or societal contexts

courses.subject: CSAT
courses.title: Arts Technology Project
courses.description: This course is a capstone project where students are required to complete an original design/research project in arts and technology under the supervision of a faculty member. The requirements may include, but are not limited to, literature review, data collection and analysis, report writing, original design, multimedia production, and project presentation or exhibition. Upon completion of this course, students will be able to plan and execute a design project in arts technology and provide evidence of their creativity and problem-solving ability to address an art tech issue.
courses.academic_group: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
courses.academic_org: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, students will be able to:
1. Plan and carry out an independent arts technology project from conception through completion with appropriate goals, workflow, and timeline.
2. Conduct research to support creative inquiry and decision-making, including theories and contextual study, and analysis of relevant precedents.
3. Apply appropriate methods of experimentation, development, and iteration to address a selected arts technology question or problem.
4. Create an original output (e.g., digital artwork, interactive installation, multimedia piece, prototype, exhibition) that demonstrates creativity, conceptual clarity, and technical competence in arts/technology
5. Synthesize and present project findings and processes clearly through written, visual, oral, or media-based communication.
6. Evaluate the project critically in relation to sustainability, ethics, and its broader cultural or social relevance.

[course format]
This course will be based on an individual project in which each student works independently under faculty supervision.

Consultation sessions can be arranged on a flexible schedule, with regular group review sessions for work-in-progress sharing and peer learning.

Final project showcase will be organised as a class effort, with potential guest reviewers from academia and professional practice.
